summary: Triggers an action in place. Never navigates.
useWhen: the interaction performs an action — submit, save, delete, open a dialog
the result stays on the current page

useInstead.when: it navigates to a URL or changes route
useInstead.why: Link renders an <a>. Middle-click, cmd-click, copy-link-address and 'open in new tab' all work on an anchor and none of them work on a button.

useInstead.when: it toggles a persistent boolean setting
useInstead.why: a toggle announces its on/off state; a button announces only its name

primary-brand.use: the single most important action in a view

primary-neutral.use: a primary action that should not carry brand colour

primary-soft.use: a primary action on a dense or already-colourful surface

secondary.use: supporting actions shown alongside a primary one

tertiary.use: low-emphasis actions — Cancel, Back, inline row actions

destructive.requires: a Modal confirmation before the action runs

success.use: confirms the end of a flow. Rarely the right answer — prefer primary-brand.

md.use: the default; forms and page-level actions

xl.use: marketing and empty-state calls to action

startIcon.note: omit Icon's `label` — the Button's own text already names it, and a labelled icon is announced twice

guarantees: the focus ring appears for keyboard focus and not for a mouse click
hover does not latch on touch devices
requires: an accessible name — `children`, or `aria-label` when the button is icon-only

antiPatterns.why: a button that navigates breaks middle-click, cmd-click and copy-link, and is announced as a button rather than a link

antiPatterns.dont: two variant="primary-brand" buttons in the same dialog
antiPatterns.do: one primary-brand, the rest secondary or tertiary
antiPatterns.why: two primaries is the same as none — nothing indicates the expected action

antiPatterns.do: open a Modal first and put the destructive Button in its footer
antiPatterns.why: irreversible actions need a confirmation step
an icon-only button with no aria-label is announced as just 'button'
onPress is React Aria's unified pointer/keyboard/touch handler. onClick works but skips the touch and keyboard normalisation the rest of the system relies on.
